verdict: Paid campaigns have been dark 11 days; organic demand is holding.
narrative: Meta advertising stopped spending on August 6th and has produced zero leads in the 11 days since, against a prior pace of roughly 2–3 leads per day. The 28-day totals — 50 leads at $25.35 per lead on $1,267 in spend — reflect the active period before the pause, not the current state. On the organic side, Google Business Profile activity held relatively steady (57 calls and 168 total actions this period), and search clicks rose nearly 15% in the most recent week, meaning demand is present with no paid channel capturing it. Separately, of the 50 leads received this period, only 36 appear as contacts in the CRM and none converted to tracked opportunities — that intake gap is being addressed alongside the campaign restart. The priority right now is getting paid campaigns back on and closing the lead-to-intake leak so new volume is properly handled when it arrives.

highlights.phrase: leads received this period, all generated before campaigns paused on August 6th
cost per lead over the 28-day window, based on the active campaign period
phone calls from your Google Business Profile this period, holding steady while paid went dark

watch_item.issue: Meta campaigns have been fully paused for 11 consecutive days, and 50 leads from the period are not showing as opportunities in the CRM — pointing to a gap between lead intake and case pipeline.
watch_item.fix: Campaign reactivation is the immediate priority, and the intake workflow is being audited so leads that arrive are correctly tracked and followed up from day one.
